page.layout: One text column, running down the page, with the printed page number and running head above it and the signature and catchword below it. The right margin shows only show-through from the reverse side, so there are no marginal notes.

main_text.p: dicuntur, componuntur, & in quæ pri-mo resolvuntur.

Elementa sunt & partes mundi in-tegrantes, & omnium mixtorum princi-pia. Zabarellæ lib. de Nat. Scient. Const. sunt duo munera Elementorum; unum, integrare hanc machinam. Alterum, ut sit materia mixti. Piccol. lib. 2. de Elem. Elementa ut suo ordine mundum constituunt, sui conservatione illum servant; suaq; ordinata partium vicissitudine, varietatum innumerarum sunt origo: ita sui cognitione & splendore cætera cuncta ex iis prodeuntia patefaciunt, & illustrant.

Simplicia dicuntur corpora, respectu Mixtorum, non quod simpliciter sint simplicia; ex materia enim & forma constant, & sic sunt composita. At non sunt ita composita, ut mixta: Elementa respiciunt Elementata, seu mixta.

p.i: Ex Elementis componuntur mixta. Ait enim Scaliger 275. omnes substantiæ, quibus tanquam principiis corpora constant, sunt Elementa. At principia illa sint essentialia & constituentia. Resolvuntur mixta in Elementa, prima resolutione, non extrema, quæ fit in materiam & formam. Ubicunq; enim mixtum resolvitur, ibi fit resolutio in Elementa: Si jam

page.notes: The scan is slightly faint in places. "Scaliger 275." is read as printed, but the number could be misread. The sign after "Ubicunq" is read as a q with a stroke, and "Ubicunq;" is the most likely form. The italic "f"-like letters are read as long s (for example "sui", "servant", "splendore"), following the rule for long s. The printed page ends mid-sentence and continues on the next page with "ulterius".
